w: His Holiness Shri Balwantsinghji Maharaj, Guru of a Sikh Sampraday met Swamishri.
Swamishri departed from Gandhinagar at 6:00 p.m.

In the evening assembly Swamishri said, "Yogiji Maharaj had visited this region several times. Gopalanand Swami - a great yogi - was born in this region. And you are privileged and fortunate because you are staying on this holy land...
" There are many attainments in life - like money, political status...
After Thakorji's darshan in the mandir, Swamishri performed puja and arti of Shivlinga in the Ganapati shrine.

In the evening assembly, the kishores presented a small drama emphasizing the need to read Satsang literature and a debate 'What does one achieve in studying!' In his blessings Swamishri underlined the importance of Para and Apara Vidya (spiritual and temporal knowledge) for a balanced life.
Before departing from Amalner, Swamishri attended the opening of 'Pramukh Swami Road' and 'Swaminarayan Chowk' by the city officials.

At 9.45 a.m., Swamishri arrived in Mohadi. Swamishri performed the pujan and arti of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and Guru Parampara in the mandir. During the assembly Shri Dhanrajbhai, a devotee of Shastriji Maharaj, welcomed Swamishri. After blessing the assembly, Swamishri visited the home of Vithal Mahajan and recalled an incident of Nirgun Swami.
At 7.35 p.m. Swamishri arrived at the 'Shri Swaminarayan Akshar Purushottam Kumar Chhatralay' in Ukai.
ph: Swamishri with veteran devotees from the time of Shastriji Maharaj
Swamishri is on his way to the old mandir
Swamishri narrates a personal incident with Mota Swami when they were here

w: At 9.20 am, Swamishri departed from Atladra and arrived in Himmatnagar at 12 noon. In the evening satsang assembly Swamishri was welcomed with a traditional dance by youths. In his blessings Swamishri explained the importance and objective of human birth.

During Swamishri’s daily morning round on the mandir terrace sadhus presented incidents from the life of Brahmanand Swami. They sang, “Sakhi Gokul gamnã chowkmã re…” Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was placed near Swamishri and sadhus played ras. Then Swamishri was given the ras sticks and the devotional programme climaxed with Swamishri striking his sticks with the sadhus’ sticks one after another.

Today Shri Kamath, chairman and MD of ICICI Bank, came for Swamishri's darshan and a meeting. Swamishri blessed him. Hearing that the Government of India had honoured him with the Padma Bhushan award, Swamishri said at once, "You have found the jewel that is God, so now you will receive other jewels like this too. But keeping to moral rules is the greatest ornament of all. And the greatest title is God's. To keep devotion amid so much activity, that is the great thing."
In Swamishri's mind, a title greater than Padma Bhushan is 'Niti Bhushan' (adorned with morality) and 'Bhakti Bhushan' (adorned with devotion).

ds.t: God may be slow, but never unjust
w: During the evening meal, sadhus who had come from America were sitting in front doing darshan. Among them, Viveknidhi Swami and Chaitanyamurti Swami told of incidents where Swamishri had divinely entered and made impossible things possible. Viveknidhi Swami said, "Sometimes the work gets done and sometimes it does not; surely the Satpurush has some purpose in that too? Even in making us wait, there must be something?"
Swamishri said, "In God's court there may be delay, but there is no injustice. Whether things happen early or late, that too is by His wish."
Bhaktikirtan Swami said, "When our patience runs out, yours begins."
Chaitanyamurti Swami said, "Were such management classes held at the school in Chansad?"

Swamishri said, "Shastriji Maharaj did all this, and he is the one doing it. What are we to do? He does the work. He gave us the command and we joined in the seva. Yogiji Maharaj's resolve joined in too, and so the work gets done. Shriji Maharaj is the doer, Shastriji Maharaj is kind, and our knowledge is true, so the work gets done."
Viveknidhi Swami said, "If someone had said ten years ago that in ten years the organisation would grow this much, no one would have believed it. One could think the same about the next ten years."

Swamishri said, "Today young and old all have such enthusiasm that even in small centres where two or five devotees gather, they start an assembly. And many are so enthusiastic that they must build a mandir. And the mandir gets built too. By God's grace the funds come and the work gets done."
Viveknidhi Swami said, "That is all your grace and your resolve."

Swamishri said, "Everything happens by Jogi Bapa's resolve. Yogiji Maharaj used to say, 'May satsang spread across the whole world, may there be thousands of sadhus.' By that resolve the work gets done, satsang spreads, and people now come forward on their own to become sadhus, and we have to say no. Such is the grace. Because of his resolve the sadhus are increasing and mandirs are being built."
Viveknidhi Swami said, "All the devotees do a lot of seva too. They serve wholeheartedly at your word."

Swamishri said, "It has gone on because of Jogi Bapa's resolve, and because sadhus like you have been prepared, the children's, teenagers' and youths' groups all happen. The devotees too have been prepared like that, and the women too."

In this way Swamishri offered the entire credit for the growth of satsang and the organisation at his guru's feet. This servant feeling, that he himself does nothing, is seen in Swamishri day and night.

st.t: U.K.’s Newly Appointed High Commissioner Marks ‘New Beginning’ With Visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi
w: The U.K. High Commissioner to India Alex Ellis visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi on Sunday, signifying the deep relationship between BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) and the United Kingdom. High Commissioner Ellis was appointed to his position earlier this month, and his visit to Akshardham comes soon after his family’s arrival to India. High Commissioner Ellis was traditionally welcomed by Gnanmunidas Swami on behalf of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, the spiritual leader of BAPS.
High Commissioner Ellis, who came to Akshardham alongside his wife and son, said the family wanted to seek blessings as they begin their tenure in India.

“I have come here today with my family to perform the rituals — puja, aarti, abhishek and darshan — to give thanks for our arrival and to hope for the best for our time here in India. I cannot think of a more auspicious place than this temple,” he said, noting the important role England’s Neasden BAPS mandir plays in the country and throughout Europe.

He spoke highly of the role Indian nationals in the United Kingdom are playing in “protecting us all from Covid-19,” and said he is looking forward to the continued partnership between India and the U.K.

The visit is part of a long tradition of friendship between the United Kingdom and BAPS, where it continues to play an active role in community service, charity and cultural activities at 15 BAPS Swaminarayan Mandirs, including the traditional Hindu mandir in Neasden, and over 50 BAPS centers. The Neasden Temple is currently serving as a public coronavirus vaccination center, serving the local community with a particular emphasis on reaching underserved populations.

High Commissioner Ellis offered his respects at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir and performed abhishek, the ceremonial pouring of sanctified water from 151 holy bodies of water on the murti of Shri Neelkanth Varni.

Along with his family, he viewed the Gajendra Peeth, which includes 148 lifelike carved stone elephants depicting messages of peace, spirituality and social harmony. They also experienced the Sanskruti Vihar exhibition – a cultural voyage that displays 10,000 years of India’s heritage and contributions to society, as well as the Sahaj Anand multimedia water show, which depicts the timeless messages of the Upanishads.
High Commission Ellis expressed appreciation for the opportunity to visit Swaminarayan Akshardham as he kicks off his time in India.
“This is a new beginning for me, and seems an auspicious day and auspicious moment to give thanks, and to think ahead and look ahead,” he said.
In his departing note, he added, “[Swaminarayan Akshardham] was a great introduction to the Hindu faith.”
